meta.scope: Colombia batch 3 — Bogotá metro + major cities, departmental layer, trade agreements (Pacific Alliance, US FTA, CAN), oil & coffee commodity anchors, education and health statistical presence.

candidates.title: Bogotá D.C. — capital statistical identity
candidates.description: Capital district and largest urban economy. Primary domain for GEIH labour and poverty cuts, with lower informal employment and lower monetary-poverty incidence than the national average.
candidates.notes: Dominant metro node. Recent GEIH: unemployment ~8.8% (below national); informal employment among the lowest of the 23 cities (~33%). Monetary poverty incidence also lower than the national urban average. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain.

candidates.title: 13 ciudades y áreas metropolitanas — statistical domain
candidates.description: Standard high-frequency geographic domain of the GEIH comprising Bogotá and the main metropolitan areas (Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla, etc.). Core urban labour and poverty reporting frame.
candidates.notes: Workhorse urban domain. Informal employment and unemployment rates for the 13 cities are the main urban benchmarks published monthly/quarterly alongside the national total.

candidates.title: Medellín Área Metropolitana — statistical profile
candidates.description: Second-largest metropolitan area. Regularly published as a distinct GEIH and poverty domain with intermediate informal-employment and poverty outcomes.
candidates.notes: Key secondary metro. Completes the capital–second-city contrast inside the national urban hierarchy.

candidates.title: Alianza del Pacífico (Protocolo Comercial)
candidates.publisher: Estados miembros de la Alianza del Pacífico (Chile, Colombia, México, Perú)
candidates.description: Regional integration initiative and commercial protocol among the four Pacific-facing Latin American economies. Preferential trade, investment and regulatory cooperation framework.
referenced_by: DANE–DIAN bilateral trade statistics with AP partners
candidates.notes: Latin American Pacific counterpart to MERCOSUR. Continuously cited in official trade reporting; bilateral trade with AP partners is tracked separately to avoid double-counting with existing bilateral FTAs.

candidates.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Colombia–Estados Unidos
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement in force since 2012. Core preferential-access instrument for the US market and a recurring reference in trade and investment analysis.
referenced_by: Export and import statistics by partner
Policy debates on US market access
candidates.notes: Major bilateral FTA. Continuously cited in official trade-performance reporting and in discussions of non-mining export diversification.

candidates.title: Comunidad Andina (CAN) — marco comercial
candidates.publisher: Estados miembros de la Comunidad Andina
candidates.description: Andean Community trade and integration framework. Long-standing preferential trade arrangement among the Andean partners.
referenced_by: MinCIT bilateral and regional trade reports
DANE–DIAN trade statistics with CAN partners
candidates.notes: Older regional instrument still operational and regularly referenced in Colombian trade statistics and policy documents.

candidates.title: Producción y exportaciones de petróleo / Mining-energy exports
candidates.publisher: DANE / Ministerio de Minas y Energía / Banrep
candidates.description: Statistics of crude-oil and broader mining-energy production and exports. Structurally important component of merchandise exports and of the external accounts.
candidates.notes: Commodity backbone of the export basket. Mining-energy share of total exports remains large; recent years have seen volume and price swings that dominate the goods-trade balance.

candidates.title: Café — producción y exportaciones
candidates.publisher: DANE / Federación Nacional de Cafeteros / MinCIT
candidates.description: Statistics of coffee production and exports. Iconic non-mining agricultural export and a recurring line in trade and rural-economy analysis.
candidates.notes: Signature soft-commodity export. Appears in both the agricultural and the non-mining-energy export aggregates and is continuously cited in rural and trade-policy discussion.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Calidad de Vida (ECV)
candidates.description: Periodic multi-purpose household survey measuring living conditions, housing, education, health affiliation, subjective well-being and access to services. Complements GEIH on non-labour dimensions of welfare.
candidates.notes: Key living-conditions survey. 2024 results cover health-service perception, education, housing deficit and subjective poverty. Published for national, Bogotá and departmental domains.

candidates.title: Pruebas Saber / ICFES learning assessments
candidates.description: National standardised assessments of student learning outcomes (Saber 11 and related). Principal learning-quality indicator for the school system.
candidates.notes: Flagship education-quality statistic. Complements enrolment and attainment data from ECV and administrative sources. Continuously cited in education-policy evaluation.

proposed_edges.basis: Bogotá is a primary geographic domain of the GEIH.
The 13-cities domain is a standard high-frequency cut of the GEIH.
Pacific Alliance preferential trade is a recurring analytical dimension of merchandise-trade reporting.
The US FTA underpins preferential bilateral trade flows that appear in the trade statistics.
Oil and mining-energy products are a major component of merchandise exports.
Coffee is a signature non-mining agricultural export line.
ECV is a core multi-purpose survey of DANE.
Saber assessments measure learning outcomes of the school population whose enrolment and attainment are characterised in the ECV.
